title: A smaller result can be a better answer
summary: An example of filtering rows with WHERE and making ordering explicit.

content.text: Example lesson: WHERE filters rows according to a condition. ORDER BY controls how the result is presented. This hypothetical query is a teaching illustration.

SELECT product_id, unit_price
FROM products
WHERE unit_price > 20
ORDER BY unit_price DESC, product_id;
The secondary ordering by product_id makes ties in price easier to inspect. Without ORDER BY, a database does not promise a particular row order.
Try it: change the condition to include prices equal to 20, then sort from the least expensive product to the most expensive.
